q: who was the most successful pirate
tell me about the most successful pirate
a: The most successful pirate in history by wealth and power was likely Zheng Yi Sao (also known as Ching Shih), a Chinese pirate who operated in the South China Sea during the early 19th century (1801-1810). At her peak, she commanded over 1,800 ships and an estimated 70,000 pirates, making her fleet larger than most national navies of the time. She successfully defeated the Chinese imperial navy, the Portuguese navy, and the British Royal Navy. Her code of laws was remarkably progressive: all captured loot was officially inventoried and distributed, and there were strict punishments for disobeying orders or stealing from the common treasury. She eventually negotiated a peaceful surrender with the Chinese government, retired with her wealth, and later ran a gambling house. In the Western world, Blackbeard (Edward Teach) was one of the most famous pirates, operating in the Caribbean and along the American coast in the early 18th century. However, his career was relatively short (1716-1718) compared to Zheng Yi Sao. Captain Henry Morgan was also highly successful but operated as a privateer (government-sanctioned pirate) and was eventually knighted and made governor of Jamaica. Bartholomew Roberts (Black Bart) captured over 400 ships during his career, making him one of the most prolific pirates by number of ships captured.
